mcts._num_simulations_note: 600. The visits-per-action argument for 1200 (140 actions / 600 sims = 4.3 visits) assumed a prior spread uniformly over 128 wall actions — wall_mask_iters removes that premise, since the masked phase has ~4 legal actions and the unmasked phase starts from a move-concentrated prior. Self-play is 93% of the iteration, so 600 roughly halves the run: N=2 ~32h vs ~62h at 150 iters.

training._iters_note: num_iterations/games_per_iteration are per variant; N=4 games run ~3x longer so it buys fewer of them for the same wall clock
training._replay_buffer_note: 100k ~= 7 iterations of coverage at N=2 — the regime runs/n2_5x5_buf10k_v1 validated.
training._ply_counted_note: max_game_moves and explore_moves both count plies, not rounds — set per variant so each player gets the same budget; see variants.n2/n4
training._discount_unit_note: Per-variant: 'round' decays per the mover's own turns, 'ply' per move by anybody. Measured better at N=2, worse at N=4.
training._accept_margin_note: 0.08 at eval_games=160. The old 0.05 at 80 games was +0.9 sigma = 19% false accepts, and v4's post-iter-15 accepts were consistent with pure noise. Sigma depends on DECIDED games, not eval_games: N=4 decides 94% (+2.3 sigma), N=2 only 78% (+1.8 sigma, ~4%) because gate games time out at max_game_moves far more than self-play games do.
training._wall_mask_note: wall_mask_fraction, NOT the phase/ramp (both now 0). Measured against probe_n2_ramp/best.pt: get_valid_actions gates walls on walls_remaining>0, so budget 1 and budget 10 are the SAME 131-action problem (3 legal at budget 0). Every ramp step above 0 was a no-op and the whole cliff is 0 -> 1. The collapse is value-coverage loss, not prior dilution: after a fully masked phase the value head has never seen a walled state, while root Dirichlet noise (eps 0.25, alpha 0.1 over 131 actions) inflates wall prior mass 0.00024 -> 0.245, so ~24% of self-play moves become near-random walls that MCTS cannot reject. 0.5 mixes wall-free and full-wall games in EVERY iteration from the first, so neither distribution is ever out of coverage. See academic_experiences.md 8.6.
training._reward_decay_note: 0.99, NOT 0.97. Probed both 5x5 arms vs greedy at tensor spec v1, 20 games/seat: gamma=0.99 goes 40/40 (seat 0 with exactly 1 wall/game), gamma=0.97 goes 20/40, losing seat 0 entirely (0/20) by over-walling at 3/game. Seat 0 is won only by spending a turn on a wall that pays off later, and a steeper discount makes that lose to advancing now. The 2026-06 gamma ablation measured loss_v drift only and says nothing about playing strength.
training._greedy_stop_note: Abort on racing decay, which the gate cannot see: in local_9x9_v6 it accepted at 69% and 60% while greedy fell 60% -> 10% over the same window. One seat is always winnable by racing alone (seat 1 at N=2, seat 0 at N=4), so the best per-seat rate has a hard ceiling and only falls if the policy stops racing. Warns on the first eval 20+ pts below the peak, stops on the second. best.pt holds the peak, so an early stop still ships the good model.
training._greedy_stop_z_note: A strike needs the drop to clear BOTH greedy_stop_drop and greedy_stop_z sigma. Without the sigma test a model whose true rate never changes aborts 53-92% of the time, because the peak is a max over seats and evals (see academic_experiences.md 8.5). At 20 games/seat only a collapse is detectable; that is what racing decay looks like.
training._greedy_min_seat_note: Companion to the decay watch, which can only fire on a fall from a peak. probe_n4_ramp peaked at 0.10 against a 0.20 drop, so a strike was arithmetically impossible and it ran 10 h past the point the answer was known. 0.25 is a deliberately low bar: after the masked phase the model should own the seat racing wins. Armed only once the mask ends, since every run is below it while untrained.
training._minimax_note: The HELD-OUT baseline. Once the opponent pool anchors on greedy, win_vs_greedy measures fit rather than generalisation, and nothing else is held out: vs_random saturates at 100% by iteration 5 and the gate is relative to a moving champion. minimax is depth-limited maxn on MovesToFinish(nearest rival) - MovesToFinish(self), the conventional Quoridor baseline, and unlike greedy it PLACES WALLS -- measured 11 wins in 12 games against greedy at 9x9 N=2 with 6.3 walls/game. Wall candidates are restricted to slots touching some player's shortest path, which is what makes depth 2 affordable: ~19 s per 40-game eval at both player counts.
training._greedy_min_seat_after_note: The floor arms at max(wall_mask_iters, this). A mixed run sets wall_mask_iters=0, so without this the floor would arm at iteration 0 and — at eval_every 4, patience 2 — could abort a healthy run at iteration 8 before it has trained. 12 gives three evals of grace.
training._eval_every_note: 4, not 5: probe_n2_ramp peaked at iteration 4 (45% vs greedy, seat 1 18/20) and the gate must land ON it to put it in best.pt. The peak is early; missing it costs the deliverable.

parallel._num_workers_note: Match the pod's cgroup cpu quota (16). Above it the jupyter server stops answering its own health check, whose entrypoint runs pkill -9 on failure.

n2._num_workers_note: 8, not the parallel section's 16, because n2 and n4 run CONCURRENTLY: 8 + 8 matches the 16-cpu cgroup quota exactly. Above the quota the jupyter server stops answering its own health check and the entrypoint pkills the run. Raise to 16 if running this variant alone.
n2._sizing_note: 60 x 80, not 150 x 160. Under the pure-masked probe the peak arrived at iteration 4, so the run is sized to reach a racer early and then keep it while walls are learned alongside — not to grind. The racing-decay and never-acquired stops end it early if the curriculum fails, so 60 is a ceiling not a plan. ~14 h at 16 workers.

n4._eval_greedy_note: 80, not 40: the greedy eval rotates the candidate through all N seats, so at N=4 a 40-game eval is only 10 games per seat — and greedy_stop_patience keys on the BEST per-seat rate, which at n=10 has SE ~0.095, making the 20-pt abort threshold barely 2 sigma. 80 gives 20/seat, matching n2, where 20-pt is ~4 sigma. Costs ~20s an eval against a ~500s iteration.
n4._sizing_note: 40 x 40, smaller than n2's 60 x 80 because N=4 games run to a 320-ply cap and cost roughly twice as much per game. Both earlier N=4 probes used the phase/ramp curriculum now known to be inert, so the mixed curriculum is untried here — this run is a real test, not a repeat. The racing-decay and never-acquired stops bound it.
